| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/bensamuels/p/the-american-tradition-of-punching?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

The last two weeks or so have been notable in the landscape of satire and comedy:
* On July 17, CBS (owned by Paramount) [cancelled](https://substack.com/redirect/82d2bf0d-d342-4a8a-99c2-d80fe980baac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) _The Late Show with Stephen Colbert_ , albeit with about a year of notice.
* On July 23, _South Park_ --a show that's never been known for its restraint--[pulled no punches making fun of Trump](https://substack.com/redirect/5fe065e0-b8b9-4261-a0be-d58790bc6868?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).1
* On July 26, Tom Lehrer, a musician and one of the great satirists of the 20th century, [died](https://substack.com/redirect/fdcde7fa-c6d6-427f-9cee-6f9927ef890b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).2

The First Amendment gives Americans [some of the strongest free speech protections](https://substack.com/redirect/b07d4ca0-a514-46bc-a7e0-996866f227f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the world. But Trump, armed with the might of the Oval Office, has sued everyone from [Facebook](https://substack.com/redirect/d54460ec-dfd2-4e37-b1d6-a8f1e06853cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to _[60 Minutes](https://substack.com/redirect/e53df389-a7b6-4a98-9dfa-8e108988e9c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ to [Columbia University](https://substack.com/redirect/b406e92b-6dc0-4cbf-a176-c3d1a83e4fb5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to [Rupert Murdoch](https://substack.com/redirect/edb41a8d-452a-4b53-bac3-59e8b7364b37?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), strong-arming concessions that weaken our right to free speech.
All of this makes comedy, satire, and punching up more important now than it's been in a while.
Said another way: thanks to _South Park_ and all of you making jokes about Donald Trump's [schvantz](https://substack.com/redirect/3a627ba4-78f1-4ff0-9bed-e541420de7e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). You're patriots of the highest order.
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9iZW5zYW11ZWxzLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9hY2NvdW50IiwicCI6MTY5NDYzMTIzLCJzIjoyNDQwMzk4LCJmIjp0cnVlLCJ1Ijo5MDUwMTE5MiwiaWF0IjoxNzUzODc4Mzg4LCJleHAiOjIwNjk0NTQzODgsImlzcyI6InB1Yi0wIiwic3ViIjoibGluay1yZWRpcmVjdCJ9.k928lFEcnfc6ik5NOd-jlfaz6pYh2syKTCcPWsYIk1k?)
> _**Article summary:**_
> * _Trump may be worse on this dimension, but unfortunately, Presidents using their office to attack the free press is a tactic about as old as the country itself._
> * _Comedians have often been more effective at calling out hypocrisy and abuses of power than traditional media --there's a rich history of that too._
> * _There are lots of fun audio and video clips throughout this post. Enjoy!_
>

### Presidents have always supported a free press...as long as it's not targeted at them
We all have a tendency to think ahistorically and note that things now are unique or worse than they've ever been. But history has a way of repeating itself, and presidents have never liked bad news. Just a few examples of that:
* John Adams used the [Sedition Act of 1798](https://substack.com/redirect/3040f8d4-6a9f-4ec6-a2a3-d9440c995e25?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to arrest newspaper publisher [Benjamin Franklin Bache](https://substack.com/redirect/7656507b-2950-4712-a892-333204f33597?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)3 for calling the President, "[Old, querulous, Bald, blind, crippled, [and] Toothless.](https://substack.com/redirect/46a81fac-2fec-4c9b-a38a-1579f8cc0ea2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)"4
* Andrew Jackson [replaced postmasters who didn't agree with his agenda](https://substack.com/redirect/78fbb02f-f5e3-4595-a11b-3d58b9b58008?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [censored anti-slavery content](https://substack.com/redirect/72bdacda-226d-4804-bffb-c6fec9dfeb62?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the mail.
* Franklin Roosevelt [had the IRS audit](https://substack.com/redirect/4c71bd7e-4f2b-4c35-a253-39118cb5a29d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [William Randolph Hearst](https://substack.com/redirect/d97138ad-e44c-4302-8354-4f42a0ce0534?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Moses Annenberg](https://substack.com/redirect/be94836f-b12a-49c2-9282-18b8f2376715?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [Charles Coughlin](https://substack.com/redirect/94205e40-f15e-4cb0-be9e-b3e0bdadfbf2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg),5 all conservative media personalities and publishers who opposed his agenda.
* John Kennedy wasn't happy with the press coverage of the _New York Herald Tribune_ and [cancelled his subscription](https://substack.com/redirect/73d4652c-84da-4c6e-b3f8-fd708f55f494?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--preferring to read the _St. Louis Post-Dispatch_ instead.
* Richard Nixon kept an "[enemies list](https://substack.com/redirect/478584bc-2ec9-4596-8fb1-b9cfcb60f3b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" that included reporters and tried to [block damaging information](https://substack.com/redirect/aa22b83d-e40e-4950-8ccc-b28718314849?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from the [Pentagon Papers](https://substack.com/redirect/8e7b10d8-6349-4884-ad97-b7f959e7e2d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from being published.

This is only a partial list; you'd be hard-pressed to find a president that _didn 't_ have an adversarial relationship with the press, at least from time to time.
Let me be clear: I'm not defending this. It's the worst of political survival instincts. But it's worth calling out that while it may be more extreme now, the tactic isn't new.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=169463123&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTY5NDYzMTIzLCJpYXQiOjE3NTM4NzgzODgsImV4cCI6MTc1NjQ3MDM4OCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.zkGWo0h5a89q9ouHdBz45t_JeiN_kvdhjr0vGVfrIwg)
### For as long as there have been U.S. presidents, there have been people making fun of them
It's no accident that the most prestigious award in comedy is literally named for [Mark Twain](https://substack.com/redirect/212b15e0-de1c-46cc-9e88-d693b89d5747?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), who regularly skewered what he saw as injustices and absurdities in American society.
Over time, people like [H. L. Mencken](https://substack.com/redirect/54517dac-be45-42f5-a0c3-6939cbcc1183?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Will Rogers](https://substack.com/redirect/a0f6e058-138d-494e-a324-f87eaf0f4780?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [Walter Winchell](https://substack.com/redirect/437a72bf-1076-4913-af25-037013455128?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--all prominent satirists and political commentators--were some of the most famous men in America in their time.6 Benjamin Franklin, as [Silence Dogood](https://substack.com/redirect/109a359a-1bc0-4dd0-8635-71b3049cca0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg),7 basically got his start writing about, and making fun of, American society.
All of this brings us to Tom Lehrer, who died last week at 97. He had a [brief run of pretty substantial fame](https://substack.com/redirect/3d1987f8-53b8-4943-b6d4-755229d5bedf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), though the last few decades of his life were spent in relative anonymity.8
But his work as a songwriter and satirist was biting and influential in his time. Here's one of my favorites, when he takes the U.S. government to task for bringing Nazi [Wernher von Braun](https://substack.com/redirect/dea1749d-5725-4f3c-b6ad-def62e3981ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)9 to work on our rocketry program in the '50s and '60s.
[| Wernher Von BraunTom Lehrer
---|---](https://substack.com/redirect/233071c7-89ff-4b26-a8cd-d9da3a45a875?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Given the era, it's no surprise that he wrote a lot about the threat of nuclear weapons too, including this song:
[| So Long, Mom (A Song For World War III)Tom Lehrer
---|---](https://substack.com/redirect/3f2cb693-fa54-483c-a927-b460c8f1e4e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
What's the lesson in all of this?
* Things rarely feel stable in the world. We've got our problems now, but in the '50s and '60s, they had more than their share to worry about: [nuclear war](https://substack.com/redirect/3110fbd4-be3a-4c82-b451-348ee2bd16e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the [Civil Rights movement](https://substack.com/redirect/dee6eb1f-3ba8-4115-b2a8-df19cc8584b3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [religious conflicts](https://substack.com/redirect/423e528d-57c9-411c-ba2b-bc813c89d0f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that don't keep as many of us today up at night.
* Political comedy--often scathing comedy--is older than the country itself.
* **Some of America 's fiercest comedy critics have been some of its proudest patriots**. [Mel Brooks](https://substack.com/redirect/0262abc4-81b6-4af4-a92c-b36b5b5b7fe9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [fought in World War II](https://substack.com/redirect/43f268e7-e17e-4724-8aad-b71dcc86e6c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and _[Blazing Saddles](https://substack.com/redirect/f25ac4fc-a5da-4a45-8d05-fd1f33154c2e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ is one of the great all-time takedowns of racism. The same could be said for [Norman Lear](https://substack.com/redirect/d4528af3-df85-47e1-a31d-229f1d2a91f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), another World War II veteran, and his show _[All in the Family](https://substack.com/redirect/48182797-892a-44a9-a59d-b35775d1febb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_.

For once, I'm not actually sure that was the case when it came to Colbert's show getting cancelled: it was reportedly [losing $40 million per year](https://substack.com/redirect/55dabacd-6b84-401c-8833-c52c18ce8e61?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Starting around 2015, they [attacked political correctness](https://substack.com/redirect/e6927c9c-d0fc-4330-af5e-8a0c73b1ff49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at a time when doing so was unpopular with the political left. Their [Scientology episode](https://substack.com/redirect/a5dbe117-ebb1-4514-9165-c71c91390717?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), among their most famous, helped [jump-start scrutiny](https://substack.com/redirect/ecad4369-b55d-4cc9-8073-3408a3f246b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and very plausibly [led to a decline in its number of followers](https://substack.com/redirect/e05fbf22-81f3-4983-aea7-16ef11d55948?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):

And _this_ was the moment when they decided to [generate one of the more immature, outrageous, outrageously funny, and NSFW deepfakes](https://substack.com/redirect/a592e9a5-0c39-412a-bd6b-5172ac8dbb39?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) you'll ever see.

### Laughter is the best medicine (and political tool)
The White House did nothing but draw attention to _South Park_ when they [put out a statement about the episode](https://substack.com/redirect/7ba1f2a8-b5fc-4647-9e8a-cec874851266?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).12 The man can't stand being insulted.13
_South Park_ , as ever, knew what they were doing. The news of these past few weeks--the extortion, the cancellations, and the thin skin--serve as an important reminder: comedy is a powerful tool that even a vengeful presidency can't impede. [Joe Rogan complimented the episode](https://substack.com/redirect/25e64a58-abf5-40cd-9fd0-edb3175dc9c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which speaks to its broad appeal.
I'm not saying people are wrong to be gloomy about the state of politics today. **But being fatalistic all the time hasn 't won people over. Democrats have been acting this way for 10 years, only to watch voters slowly move away from them.**
Comedy can be a powerful tool, and when it's done well, it's an effective way to speak truth to power.
Tom Lehrer understood that. Colbert and _South Park_ do too. We all could learn something from them.

subject: Rush your signed petition to President Trump
body:
I’m writing to you today because a Soros-funded prosecutor is trying to lock my police officer husband up for the next 11 years for saving a fellow officer’s life.

| | |
---
Dear Friend,I’m writing to you today because a Soros-funded prosecutor is trying to lock my police officer husband up for the next 11 years for saving a fellow officer’s life. **[And your petition to President Donald Trump is my last chance to save my family from being torn apart.](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2zkif2aj5mh10q7d5mhr0k9dskck6cifoqjvd108o_rp22sh2s8i6epb6c3ieco30cdh2bs)**
---
[](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2z921suqblnbmibp3gqclangsrl2cfsp5qhsm85pg_rp22sh2s8i6epb6c3ieco30cdh2bs)
---
The picture I’ve sent you is of Brad with our two boys. To them, he’s not just their dad – he’s their hero. Friend, in 10 years as an officer with the Las Cruces Police Department, my husband had never fired his service weapon on the line of duty. But when his partner was lying stunned on the pavement – and the robbery suspect who knocked him down and tried to take his service weapon was aiming the officer’s stolen taser right at him... ...Brad knew he had no choice. He drew his pistol and fired a single shot, killing the suspect and saving his partner’s life. When Brad got home and told me what happened, I couldn’t stop crying. I was so grateful he was alive. And when an Internal Investigation and the local District Attorney cleared Brad of any wrongdoing, I thought this awful episode was behind us. I couldn’t have been more wrong. Because more than a year after the incident, the New Mexico Attorney General, Raul Torrez, charged my husband with Voluntary Manslaughter! You see, Raul Torrez is an out-of-control prosecutor who hates the police. His campaign was funded by leftist billionaire George Soros. And he’s determined to make a name for himself by destroying Brad. He even held a press conference and turned the microphone over to the suspect’s family so they could spread hateful lies about my husband, smearing him as a “racist” and a “cold-blooded killer.” It only got worse at the trial. And when the jury declared my husband guilty and Brad was led off to jail, it felt like our lives were over. But my heartbreak turned into rage when I found out two details weeks after the trial ended:
---
**#1. During the trial, the judge accidentally dismissed two jurors Brad’s legal team had chosen during jury selection, replacing them with alternates. ** **#2. One of the jurors was secretly an outspoken anti-police activist. **
---
Friend, this juror is a member of a radical anti-police group. They even participated in anti-police protests. And during jury selection, they failed to disclose any of this. In a sane world, this should have been enough to force Raul Torrez to request a re-trial – or drop the case completely. But that’s not the world we live in. Instead, he’s fighting all the way to the New Mexico Supreme Court to protect this lying juror and keep my husband’s unjust conviction in place. **[That’s why I’m asking you to sign the enclosed petition to President Trump.](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2ztpuek4unlippu3q5cesjan52tbkfn3e96dsdgco_rp22sh2s8i6epb6c3ieco30cdh2bs)** Because if it wasn’t clear before, it is now... This was never about justice. It’s a politicized witch hunt of an innocent man just because he worse a badge. President Trump calls it “lawfare.” And the only way to put a stop to it is good people like you standing up for my husband and saying “NO MORE!” With your petition, you’re asking President Trump to order his Department of Justice to open an investigation into the unjust, politically motivated prosecution of my husband. **[Please take just a minute right now to sign and submit your petition.](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2zt4u6fa61e69pf52l03v9aasua70ftbmc2rv7ic8_rp22sh2s8i6epb6c3ieco30cdh2bs)** Because my husband doesn’t deserve this. He’s an honorable man who wanted nothing more than to serve his country and his community. That’s why he served for 3 years in the Army as a cavalry scout. And it’s why he served for 10 years as a police officer. But more than that, he’s a wonderful husband and incredible father to our 9- and 6- year-old sons. We’ve tried to explain to our boys as best we can about what’s going on. But they’re too young to fully understand. And I can’t bear to think of what it will do to them if they’re forced to grow up with him behind bars. But that’s exactly what will happen if Raul Torrez gets his way. For a long time, stopping this witch hunt seemed impossible. But thank God, we got a call from Jason Johnson. Jason is a retired police officer – and he’s the President of the Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund (LELDF). If you’ve ever heard of LELDF, you know they’re a national group fighting on behalf of wrongfully-accused police officers...like Brad. LELDF has helped dozens of innocent officers – and their families – when it seemed like there was no hope left. And with the thought of losing my husband and trying to suddenly raise my two boys on my own – I was certainly hopeless. LELDF is helping my husband get the legal defense he deserves by paying for the best lawyers and expert witnesses available. And they’re also helping fund this petition drive to President Trump. LELDF was an answer to prayer for our family. And today I’m hoping you’ll be an answer to prayer too. **[When you submit your signed petition...would you please send in a contribution today to LELDF to help defend my husband?](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2zk2u2t2masrll90003j7ums9lt467nkud16e56i8_rp22sh2s8i6epb6c3ieco30cdh2bs)** Any amount – $35, $50, $100, or even $500 or more – will help. Because LELDF is a nonprofit, your gift is tax-deductible too. But whatever you can give, **[the most important thing is that you rush back your signed petition and your tax-deductible gift as soon as you can – right now if possible.](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2zu5saglorne4qm6itce505sdi7a32uvpbqjphhs8_rp22sh2s8i6epb6c3ieco30cdh2bs)** I need to deliver your petition to President Trump as soon as possible. And your petition and $35 gift could be the difference between stopping this witch hunt... ...or my husband spending the next 11 years behind bars. I’m sorry this email wound up being so long. Thank you for taking the time to read it today. And thank you in advance for helping defend my Brad from this witch hunt.
---
Sincerely,
---
Lacy Lunsford
---
P.S. The last three years have been a never-ending nightmare for my family. And right now, you’re our only hope. **[Please rush back your signed petition to President Trump and your tax-deductible gift of $35 or more as soon as you can.](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2zhsa6g6kjvg8duah12d6kk6j3s3ptd2khfv8cgag_rp22sh2s8i6epb6c3ieco30cdh2bs)** My husband doesn’t deserve to spend the next 11 years in prison for saving a fellow officer’s life. And my boys don’t deserve to have their father locked up. If he’s ripped away from us, they’ll never recover. Thank you for doing what you can to help our family!
---

And, for a limited time, we'll also send you a free color map of the Roman world at the end of the Republic. This map is a helpful companion to the course DVD and will illustrate many of the topics discussed in the lectures. Simply use this secure link to reserve your DVD box set of " The Rise and Fall of the Roman Republic," along with the companion map today: By studying ancient Rome, you'll discover the conditions necessary to preserve a republic, and, conversely, how a republic may lose its way. That's why we produced " The Rise and Fall of the Roman Republic" and why I hope you'll watch and share the course on DVD. Thank you for helping to preserve liberty for future generations of Americans through education with Hillsdale College! In the 2022 election for this seat, Republican John James won by 0.5% – not even a full 1%. Now, John James is running for Governor, which makes this an open and highly competitive seat. All of the other U.S. House races in swing districts have Republican incumbents, which makes it tougher for a Democrat to break through.

In 2018, John James said he is “100% Pro-Life” and compared abortion to “genocide.” Most recently, **Representative James proudly voted YES on Trump’s “Big Beautiful Bill** ,” which is one of the worst bills to become law in modern history.

Here’s how Christina responded:

_“The Republicans passed their bill. It's a direct hit to the people who work the hardest and carry the heaviest burdens – and it will make life more expensive for almost all of us. As a prosecutor and as an advocate, I believe that public servants are supposed to work FOR the people, not against them.

I’m running for Congress because I want to make sure my neighbors - the working families in our community - have affordable healthcare, housing, groceries, and daycare. We have a lot of work to do, but together, we can continue to fight for a better future.” _**

Larry Sabato’s ‘Crystal Ball’ has rated MI-10 as a Tossup in 2026, and this district is one of the DCCC’s targeted races for 2026.** When Christina was on the ballot as the Democratic Nominee for County Prosecutor in 2024, she **outperformed** both the Democratic congressional nominee AND Kamala Harris. Now, it's time to ensure she has what she needs to replace John James and get us a step closer to regaining control of the House.

**This is our _most realistic opportunity_ of the entire 2026 cycle to flip a House seat from red to blue – and we need your help to make that happen.**

[****This is the time that Christina needs the most help, as institutional support groups are evaluating where to invest. Help us ensure Christina has what she needs to catch up to her all-male opponents and get her as much attention as possible by rushing a contribution to her campaign today. →**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/hbm-hines/?refcode=EM_F_250730Tossup_N_EH_90DO_11_G_N_L2&amount=20.26)

Together,

Erica Henry

Gov. Mike Braun and other Indiana leaders hosted visitors from Washington as the head of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and U.S. secretary of energy came to town for a big announcement they characterized could lead to the largest deregulatory action in U.S. history. The announcement came against the backdrop of one of the country's oldest truck manufacturers, Kenworth. That's where U.S. EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin announced a proposal to get rid of regulations that limit the amount of greenhouse gas emissions trucks and cars can produce in the United States. The standards on vehicle emissions were put in place in 2009 after the EPA determined that carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases endangered public health and contributed to global climate change. The regulations came as a result of something called "the endangerment finding" that said climate change is a threat to public health, leading to climate regulations under the Clean Air Act. The proposal announced by the EPA would roll those regulations back. "The fact that we're pivoting here in 2025 and it's in our own state of Indiana, I'd say, 'Hallelujah,'" Braun told those gathered. "This proposed rule is a proposal to eliminate the endangerment finding to eliminate greenhouse gas standards, all the regulations that came out, including the electronic vehicle mandates," said Zeldin. The president of the Indiana Trucking Association said electric vehicle mandates were an economic burden on the trucking industry. "That mandate forced a single unproven technology onto an extremely complex and varied industry where one size does not fit all," said Gary Langston. "Can you imagine how much cargo we could transport around the country if you could only use an electric truck," asked U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright. "We want to get back to science and data and facts," Wright added, announcing the release of a report on Tuesday on the Department of Energy's website. Wright said the report came after a study by five scientists on climate change, saying the report had been through an internal peer review at the Department of Energy and national labs. He said the practical application of rolling back emission regulations would lead to a lower cost on vehicles. "Electric vehicles are not climate tools, but politically popular because rich people like them, so they've been deemed climate solutions," Wright said. But here’s the truth — I’ve got something they don’t. I’ve got people power. I’ve got the youth. The disaffected. The folks who’ve gone without — who hear my message and feel seen. I’ve had so many people come up to me at town halls and community events and say, _“I’ve never heard someone speak like that. You’re giving me hope again.”_ But the tough part? Most of those people are working two or three jobs just to make ends meet. They’re living on fixed incomes. They’re spending everything they have on housing, food, and childcare. They’d give the world — but they simply can’t afford to. **I get it. I really do.** I hate money in politics. Always have. And when I get to Washington, I’m not going to forget where I came from or who sent me there. I’ll fight like hell to:
* Overturn _Citizens United_
* Pass public election financing
* And make politicians earn your vote again — not earn the backing of Wall Street and corporate America

But right now, I’ve got to meet a brutal end-of-month fundraising deadline. July’s always rough — people are out of town, budgets are tight, and it’s easy for grassroots campaigns like mine to fall behind. clean_body: | | | Friend, I need to be real with you. I’m being outraised by a candidate who doesn’t even live in this district. And that’s because every cycle, people in D.C. think this seat is for sale. But here’s the truth — I’ve got something they don’t. I’ve got people power. I’ve got the youth. The disaffected. The folks who’ve gone without — who hear my message and feel seen. I’ve had so many people come up to me at town halls and community events and say, “I’ve never heard someone speak like that. You’re giving me hope again.” But the tough part? Most of those people are working two or three jobs just to make ends meet. They’re living on fixed incomes. They’re spending everything they have on housing, food, and childcare. They’d give the world — but they simply can’t afford to. I get it. I really do. I hate money in politics. Always have. And when I get to Washington, I’m not going to forget where I came from or who sent me there. I’ll fight like hell to: Overturn Citizens United Pass public election financing And make politicians earn your vote again — not earn the backing of Wall Street and corporate America But right now, I’ve got to meet a brutal end-of-month fundraising deadline. body:
Peter,

Today, I filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration to stop its outrageous attempt to seize the private data of Minnesotans who receive help to feed themselves and their families.

The administration is demanding that states hand over sensitive personal information about millions of SNAP recipients—including their Social Security numbers and home addresses. If we refuse, they’re threatening to withhold critical SNAP funding, which over 400,000 Minnesotans rely on to put food on the table.

This is a direct threat to Minnesotans’ privacy. Federal and state laws prohibit sharing SNAP data unless it’s strictly necessary—and this is anything but. That’s why I joined a coalition of 22 states to take the Trump administration to court and stop this thinly veiled attempt to seize personal information that could be weaponized to target immigrants and other vulnerable communities.

This isn’t the first time I’ve stepped up to defend your right to privacy. Earlier this year, I sued the Trump administration to block Elon Musk and his so-called DOGE team from accessing sensitive information. And starting this Thursday, my office will begin enforcing the Minnesota Consumer Data Privacy Act—a new law that gives Minnesotans greater freedom to control their data.

I won’t let anyone violate your right to privacy or exploit sensitive information for their own nefarious purposes.

But I need your help as well, Peter. We have less than 48 hours to reach our end-of-month fundraising goal, and we’re still $14,652 short.

Our records indicate that you’re eligible for Minnesota’s Political Contribution Refund (PCR) program. That means you can donate up to $75 (or $150 for couples) and get a full refund from the state.

Will you make a fully refundable $75 donation to help me stop the Trump administration and fight for Minnesotans’ privacy?

Friend — A lot of politicians choose to do things the easy way.
They play it safe. They make nice with the powers-that-be. They don’t rock the boat or go out on a limb to fight for something, even when they know it’s the right thing to do.
**But Ilhan is different.** Whether it’s proudly supporting Medicare-for-All, or being one of the few members of Congress to vote against any and all military aid to Israel, Ilhan isn’t afraid to go against the establishment to represent the values of her constituents in Minneapolis.
The same goes for fundraising, too.
The easiest way to get elected is to cozy up to corporate special interests and billionaire mega-donors. They spend big on your campaign, and in exchange you pick up the phone when they have opinions on a big vote. And that’s how many people do it.
Ilhan, however, rejects the entire corrupt system that enables the mega-rich to buy our elections. Her campaign is powered by regular folks who believe in our mission. **That’s why our average donation so far this year is only $18.**
And that’s why Ilhan can't be unafraid when speaking out against injustice. Because she knows she has a huge team behind her to back her up.

Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene **[went off at Democrat Rep. Jasmine Crockett](https://substack.com/redirect/f6ab2f10-6c77-432d-908f-f309fa24296c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for calling Republicans hypocrites for trying to eliminate left-wing ideological government programs while allegedly enacting the "radical" Heritage Foundation's Project 2025.
MTG lets her have it...
[Click To Watch Video](https://substack.com/redirect/f6ab2f10-6c77-432d-908f-f309fa24296c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/f6ab2f10-6c77-432d-908f-f309fa24296c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
"We are living through the hell of Project 2025 right now!" Crockett claimed. "And something tells me that that's a bit of a partisan thing because they've said it's "the conservative playbook!'"
Greene fired back, "For the record, the Heritage Foundation receives no federal funding!"
**["The American taxpayer's dollars are being laundered](https://substack.com/redirect/f6ab2f10-6c77-432d-908f-f309fa24296c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** through the revolving doors of NGOs and Democrat officials," Greene continued. "To be clear, we support charitable NGOs,... We do not support politically connected NGOs who rake in billions of federal tax dollars to serve the Democrat party and their friends and their priorities!"
Watch the fiery confrontation here:
[Click To Watch Video](https://substack.com/redirect/f6ab2f10-6c77-432d-908f-f309fa24296c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

**[That's what we source at the Bonner Private Wine Partnership.](https://substack.com/redirect/b7d8f93d-d9a2-465c-82dd-965f2020769b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

These wines aren't for sale in stores, and they'll never be featured on a celebrity's Instagram.
They're for people like you. Folks who still believe in hard work, tradition, and doing things the right way.
**[See What's Inside the Box - Join Now](https://substack.com/redirect/b7d8f93d-d9a2-465c-82dd-965f2020769b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
You won't find these wines at Costco. And that's a good thing.
- Will Bonner

Most of the emails will tell you it’s an important deadline, but they will rarely explain why these End-of-Month deadlines are so critical to a campaign’s success. That’s why I wanted to take a minute and break down why our Thursday deadline is so important and more than just a marketing gimmick. Democrats are outspending Republicans by historic margins across the country, in races that wouldn’t have been considered battleground races just a few years ago. They’re relying on a radical base of megadonors and extremist special interest groups to fuel their campaigns. We don’t have their base of extremist megadonors. We’re a grassroots-powered campaign. That means, to compete every ad and voter outreach campaign needs to be carefully planned, budgeted for, and executed. Months in advance, my campaign team sets specific fundraising monthly benchmarks to run the ads and target voters we need to secure victory. These fundraising targets allow my team to plan our winning voter outreach strategy, combating anything the Democrats throw at us. In a race this expensive and contentious, every End-of-Month fundraising deadline counts. One down month or missed deadline could permanently put us on the defensive, jeopardizing our Republican Majority. I know it doesn’t sound like a lot, but with the amount Democrats are spending against us, EVERY dollar matters. subject: Fwd: Peter, you’re invited to join our summer book club!
body:
Hi Peter,
I wanted to make sure you saw my invite to our summer book club! This year we’re reading Love Your Mother by Mallory McDuff [https://mallorymcduff.com/books] for our equity summer learning project with all of our staff, and would love for you to join us for a wrap-up discussion in September. If you’d like to be a part of our book club, we invite you to sign up [https://secure.everyaction.com/g1LQKAuWDUG8CO5kydwjDQ2] and purchase the book soon!
Sign up for our Book Club [https://secure.everyaction.com/g1LQKAuWDUG8CO5kydwjDQ2?contactdata=NP5vU8fmK1xRnVhwDTP8HuUZkjx0D+J6vx8bUBX85HlL241D7AmZIJzO7xc4iHULIv9ocnUs016MURLWDQf+V74ugPhvQJDzsMVviHI1h4QUAVY5+TLMklcqm2tqZJPj]
All of us have thoroughly enjoyed reading this book so far. It is full of inspiring and enlightening stories, which is exactly the kind of book we needed this summer! Even if you aren’t able to join this summer’s book club, I hope you’ll get your hands on it at some point.
Sincerely,
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AVLCV/1/70877/images/Sarah%20Signature.png]

| Peter,

This month marked my 29th anniversary of becoming a naturalized citizen, and I couldn’t be prouder to be an American.

When my family immigrated here when I was just three years old, we faced financial hardship, language barriers, and made countless sacrifices. But in just one generation, I’m proud to have achieved my American Dream – and now, I’m running for Congress to make sure others have the same opportunity.

Right now, our immigration system is broken. But terrorizing communities and deporting American citizens – including sick children – **is not right.** We need bipartisan reform that creates strong borders, supports businesses, and a legal, safe, efficient, and humane path to citizenship.

That’s why I’m running for Congress: to fix the problems we all face, **not to play political games with people’s lives.** I believe loving your country means creating solutions to make it a better place, not tearing it apart with extremist rhetoric. I’m proud to be an American, and I’m proud of the movement that we’re building towards a better country – for everyone.

Thank you for standing with me,

Carol Obando-Derstine

There's a lot of conflicting polling and narratives out there about the Democratic Party and our strength--or weakness--heading into the midterms next year. I want to take a minute to unpack how I'm thinking about this moment, given the data we have...
_I 'm committed to keeping Endless Urgency free for everyone--but I rely on paid subscribers (starting at just $8/month) to keep it going. If you find value in the work, consider becoming a paid subscriber._
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..2tmXyAIm7MZc0njzBdoKDh7tl4Enru4EhwbXstpTjaM?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=169671036)
A new _Wall Street Journal_ poll shows Democrats have a major brand problem. Very few voters trust us on the biggest issues facing the country--outside of health care. The party is, frankly, historically unpopular in my lifetime. People are frustrated, and rightly so. I believe that's due in large part to Joe Biden's unpopularity as he left office, combined with early missteps from the establishment responding to Donald Trump's destructive first 100 days.
But then you get this second data point from CNN this weekend, which in many ways feels at odds with the first: 70% of Democrats say they're motivated to vote in the midterms, while only about half of Republicans say the same.
Then there's the third point: Trump's approval rating is faltering. CBS has him dropping from 53% when he took office to 42% now. I've seen it lower--into the upper 30s. I still think there's a "honeymoon" effect happening. People want to believe he's going to lower prices, help them buy a house, get food on the table, retire with some dignity.
I don't believe he will, of course. He intends to gaslight the American people into believing prices and inflation are down when they objectively aren't. And according to Fox News's own polling last week, he's at -30% on inflation--which is the top issue in the country. That's as bad as Biden ever was, and we're only six months into this.
_I 'm committed to keeping Endless Urgency free for everyone--but I rely on paid subscribers (starting at just $8/month) to keep it going. If you find value in the work, consider becoming a paid subscriber._
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..2tmXyAIm7MZc0njzBdoKDh7tl4Enru4EhwbXstpTjaM?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=169671036)
So what's actually happening here?
The mainstream media's narrative says the Democratic Party is broken, fractured, and in deep trouble for the midterms. I don't buy that. Just because people are mad at the Democratic Party leadership doesn't mean they're not going to vote for Democratic candidates. Anger is one of the most powerful drivers of turnout, and people are pissed about Trump.
Remember 2010? Barack Obama didn't lose the House because the GOP was suddenly beloved just two years after George W. Bush crashed the economy. He lost because a wave of economic anxiety--yes, with racial undercurrents--crashed through the electorate, and Republicans surfed it back into power. That wave didn't make them more popular. It made them temporary winners (only to lose to Obama again in 2012 after they were certain the rise of the Tea Party would bring them back into the White House--ask my new BFF, Joe Walsh, about it).
Fast-forward to now. People may not be happy with the Democratic establishment and have serious doubts about our ability to improve their lives. They may not trust or like some of the candidates we're putting forward. But that doesn't mean they want to give Republicans a blank check--or that they're going to tolerate the destruction and corruption in Washington. Voters are pissed about what's happening in the country--especially on affordability--and many of them will vote to restore balance, even if they're mad at us.
_I 'm committed to keeping Endless Urgency free for everyone--but I rely on paid subscribers (starting at just $8/month) to keep it going. If you find value in the work, consider becoming a paid subscriber._
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..2tmXyAIm7MZc0njzBdoKDh7tl4Enru4EhwbXstpTjaM?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=169671036)
Here's what I think is coming in 2026: not a full-on "Democratic Tea Party," but definitely an insurgent wave in the primaries. Some establishment-backed candidates are going to underperform--or lose outright. We'll see more surprises than I think are baked in. New voices will rise, and we'll inch closer to the new Democratic Party we're building in real time.
And we're going to see more candidates openly challenging the party's perceived establishment. They'll try to build brands that rise above it. That's smart politics--even if the Democratic Party was popular. As much as party identity matters, candidate identity matters more. A candidate who can define themselves beyond "generic Democrat" is going to perform better--full stop.
That said, we're going to have messy primaries. Some of the "it's their turn" candidates will lose. Not all--money and super PACs still exist and are a barrier to entry for many outside candidates--but enough that the trend will be obvious. And primary voters will reward candidates who don't run away from the party, but instead redefine what it means to be a Democrat on their own terms.
Come November, after some messy primaries and lots of silly intra-party fights on X, I believe we'll see a unified Democratic Party--energized by a block of high-propensity voters and backed by independents, especially younger ones, who are furious about what they're seeing and experiencing. Trump's numbers with young people--even young men--are horrendous. If they vote, and I think they will, they'll vote for Democratic candidates.
_I 'm committed to keeping Endless Urgency free for everyone--but I rely on paid subscribers (starting at just $8/month) to keep it going. If you find value in the work, consider becoming a paid subscriber._
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..2tmXyAIm7MZc0njzBdoKDh7tl4Enru4EhwbXstpTjaM?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=169671036)
But let's be clear: if we win the midterms, it won't mean the Democratic Party is "back." It won't mean we've fixed the brand. It won't mean we're suddenly in a strong position for 2028, just like 2010 didn't mean the Republicans were going to win in 2012.
It will mean that Democrats took power back because people were angry. Because we elevated candidates who rose above the party brand. Because we built better campaigns (and believe it or not, I do believe Democrats run better campaigns than Republicans on average).
And from that position, we'll have to be very careful and strategic about who we nominate in 2028. Because that person will become the standard bearer who defines what it means to be a Democrat going forward. That's when the party's brand numbers will shift--for better or worse.
I'm not using this space to push a specific candidate. I think they'll emerge in the primary, and I trust voters to make that choice (disclosure: I will surely be working for one of the campaigns in some capacity, but I don't know whom). But we've seen this movie before. Think back to 2006 and 2007. The party was lost, disorganized, unsure of itself. We had a messy primary, and from it emerged Barack Obama--the best political talent in my lifetime.
We can do that again. We have to do that again.

Democrats have brand issues, but anger is a powerful drive of turnout. | | | Jul 30 | | | | | | | | | | | | There's a lot of conflicting polling and narratives out there about the Democratic Party and our strength--or weakness--heading into the midterms next year. I want to take a minute to unpack how I'm thinking about this moment, given the data we have... I 'm committed to keeping Endless Urgency free for everyone--but I rely on paid subscribers (starting at just $8/month) to keep it going. If you find value in the work, consider becoming a paid subscriber. A new Wall Street Journal poll shows Democrats have a major brand problem. Very few voters trust us on the biggest issues facing the country--outside of health care. The party is, frankly, historically unpopular in my lifetime. People are frustrated, and rightly so. I believe that's due in large part to Joe Biden's unpopularity as he left office, combined with early missteps from the establishment responding to Donald Trump's destructive first 100 days. But then you get this second data point from CNN this weekend, which in many ways feels at odds with the first: 70% of Democrats say they're motivated to vote in the midterms, while only about half of Republicans say the same. Then there's the third point: Trump's approval rating is faltering. CBS has him dropping from 53% when he took office to 42% now. I've seen it lower--into the upper 30s. I still think there's a "honeymoon" effect happening. People want to believe he's going to lower prices, help them buy a house, get food on the table, retire with some dignity. I don't believe he will, of course. He intends to gaslight the American people into believing prices and inflation are down when they objectively aren't. And according to Fox News's own polling last week, he's at -30% on inflation--which is the top issue in the country. That's as bad as Biden ever was, and we're only six months into this. I 'm committed to keeping Endless Urgency free for everyone--but I rely on paid subscribers (starting at just $8/month) to keep it going. If you find value in the work, consider becoming a paid subscriber. So what's actually happening here? The mainstream media's narrative says the Democratic Party is broken, fractured, and in deep trouble for the midterms. I don't buy that. Just because people are mad at the Democratic Party leadership doesn't mean they're not going to vote for Democratic candidates. Anger is one of the most powerful drivers of turnout, and people are pissed about Trump. Remember 2010? Barack Obama didn't lose the House because the GOP was suddenly beloved just two years after George W. Bush crashed the economy. He lost because a wave of economic anxiety--yes, with racial undercurrents--crashed through the electorate, and Republicans surfed it back into power. That wave didn't make them more popular. It made them temporary winners (only to lose to Obama again in 2012 after they were certain the rise of the Tea Party would bring them back into the White House--ask my new BFF, Joe Walsh, about it). Fast-forward to now. People may not be happy with the Democratic establishment and have serious doubts about our ability to improve their lives. They may not trust or like some of the candidates we're putting forward. But that doesn't mean they want to give Republicans a blank check--or that they're going to tolerate the destruction and corruption in Washington. Voters are pissed about what's happening in the country--especially on affordability--and many of them will vote to restore balance, even if they're mad at us. I 'm committed to keeping Endless Urgency free for everyone--but I rely on paid subscribers (starting at just $8/month) to keep it going. If you find value in the work, consider becoming a paid subscriber. Here's what I think is coming in 2026: not a full-on "Democratic Tea Party," but definitely an insurgent wave in the primaries. Some establishment-backed candidates are going to underperform--or lose outright. We'll see more surprises than I think are baked in. New voices will rise, and we'll inch closer to the new Democratic Party we're building in real time. And we're going to see more candidates openly challenging the party's perceived establishment. They'll try to build brands that rise above it. That's smart politics--even if the Democratic Party was popular. As much as party identity matters, candidate identity matters more. A candidate who can define themselves beyond "generic Democrat" is going to perform better--full stop. That said, we're going to have messy primaries. Some of the "it's their turn" candidates will lose. Not all--money and super PACs still exist and are a barrier to entry for many outside candidates--but enough that the trend will be obvious. And primary voters will reward candidates who don't run away from the party, but instead redefine what it means to be a Democrat on their own terms. Come November, after some messy primaries and lots of silly intra-party fights on X, I believe we'll see a unified Democratic Party--energized by a block of high-propensity voters and backed by independents, especially younger ones, who are furious about what they're seeing and experiencing. Trump's numbers with young people--even young men--are horrendous. If they vote, and I think they will, they'll vote for Democratic candidates. I 'm committed to keeping Endless Urgency free for everyone--but I rely on paid subscribers (starting at just $8/month) to keep it going. If you find value in the work, consider becoming a paid subscriber. But let's be clear: if we win the midterms, it won't mean the Democratic Party is "back." It won't mean we've fixed the brand. It won't mean we're suddenly in a strong position for 2028, just like 2010 didn't mean the Republicans were going to win in 2012. It will mean that Democrats took power back because people were angry. Because we elevated candidates who rose above the party brand. Because we built better campaigns (and believe it or not, I do believe Democrats run better campaigns than Republicans on average). And from that position, we'll have to be very careful and strategic about who we nominate in 2028. Because that person will become the standard bearer who defines what it means to be a Democrat going forward. That's when the party's brand numbers will shift--for better or worse. I'm not using this space to push a specific candidate. I think they'll emerge in the primary, and I trust voters to make that choice (disclosure: I will surely be working for one of the campaigns in some capacity, but I don't know whom). But we've seen this movie before. Think back to 2006 and 2007. The party was lost, disorganized, unsure of itself. We had a messy primary, and from it emerged Barack Obama--the best political talent in my lifetime. We can do that again. We have to do that again. Tina came out as a lesbian in her early twenties and learned through her journey that advocating for herself and others was necessary to rise above intolerance and build a just world for everyone. This commitment inspired her efforts in graduate school to fight for and win domestic partnership rights for students and faculty at the University of Washington. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/112420524/560429504/-773863328?refcode=AU_TK_FR_GEN_EOM_AC_20240730_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxNjBhNmNjZi01ZDZkLWYwMTEtOGRjOS02MDQ1YmRhOWQ5NmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=34mCsC6jL8Oxo_ivb66fsZzrVXglsxCiMp-U5Rkqfew=) After graduate school, Tina returned to Oregon and joined the team at Oregon Food Bank. During her time there, she honed her skills as an advocate for others who have been overlooked and underserved. She continued her advocacy work as the policy director at Children First for Oregon (now Our Children Oregon). Her experience working with nonprofits on behalf of Oregon’s most vulnerable led her to run and serve in the Oregon Legislature. In 2013, Tina became the Oregon Speaker of the House. Through her leadership, the Oregon House passed progressive policies that expanded economic security for more families, combated climate change, and helped families in need during the pandemic. subject: How we can still win abundant, affordable housing that cuts pollution
disclaimer_text: paid for by Evergreen Action
body:
See part three of our winning strategy
| | | | [](https://actnow.evergreenaction.com/s/3828512/87SdQ4wZ) |
---|---|---
---
| Hi Friend,

Trump’s budget law is the biggest giveaway to billionaire polluters in history—packed not only with cuts to clean energy programs, food assistance, and health care, but also to impactful household efficiency incentives that help renters and homebuyers alike.

With millions of Americans already struggling to keep up with rising household costs, **this budget adds insult to injury by robbing people of funding that could be used to make their homes more efficient and affordable.** Instead, we should be implementing policies that lower transportation and home operation costs, which can save us money while also reducing toxic air pollution.

To address the housing and energy affordability crisis, **Evergreen is ramping up our work on building electrification, lower electricity rates, and abundant, affordable housing.**

Together with our priorities to get more affordable clean energy online and make transportation cleaner and more affordable, this is the third leg of our ambitious state-level policy agenda that will help lay the groundwork for future federal ambition.

But with an important fundraising deadline coming up on **July 31** — _just one day away_ —**we need your help to make sure we have the resources to see these plans through.**[**Will you make a gift to Evergreen now to fuel our campaigns on energy, transportation, and housing affordability?**](https://actnow.evergreenaction.com/s/3828513/87SdQ4wZ) |
---
[DONATE TODAY](https://actnow.evergreenaction.com/s/3828514/87SdQ4wZ)
---
---
| By expanding available housing and implementing policies that decrease transportation and energy costs, we can improve affordability while also reducing pollution from buildings. In fact, it’s estimated that equitably electrifying homes could save U.S. households a total of **$96 billion through reduced utility bills over the next 25 years.** These upgraded homes can reduce climate pollution by up to 72 percent and reduce indoor air pollution by 50 percent.

**To get there, we have a plan. It involves:** |
---
|
* **Collaborating with partners** in the affordable housing sector and the abundant housing movement to develop a shared vision and policy suite that meet the current political dynamics found in target states like Michigan and Pennsylvania.
* **Shaping the narrative that energy and housing affordability go hand in hand** , specifically by targeting sympathetic state lawmakers, governors, and media.
* **Providing state leaders with actionable policy recommendations** —like a Clean Heat Standard or Energy Efficient Resource Standard—which consistently fund whole home energy efficiency and electrification upgrades while setting standards to reduce pollution from buildings.
* **Advocating for policies like a Zero Emissions Heating Equipment Standard** that will drive an increase in the heat pump market share and lead to an eventual phase-out of pollution-emitting equipment.

|
---
| We anticipate being up against forces like NIMBYism, fossil fuel companies, and gas utilities every step of the way, and we need to be prepared to fight back. **We have a real and impactful opportunity to turn the tide on the affordability crisis, and it starts right now, with your support.**

Our goal is to raise **$15,000 by midnight on Thursday** , which will fuel the strategies, resources, and organizing needed in this next chapter of our work. [**Please help us get there by making a contribution today.**](https://actnow.evergreenaction.com/s/3828515/87SdQ4wZ) |
---
[POWER OUR WORK](https://actnow.evergreenaction.com/s/3828516/87SdQ4wZ)
---
---
| Thank you for your unwavering commitment to this cause. |
---

---
### Tony Sirna

Evergreen Action

name: Mikie Sherrill
body:
Peter, it’s been a
few weeks since I won the Democratic nomination for governor of New
Jersey. But this race is already a rollercoaster — we’ve seen an
outpouring of grassroots support and also faced a barrage of right-wing
attacks.

Today, I need your help to stop MAGA Republicans from flipping New Jersey
red, and I’m humbly asking you to [ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20250730-2?refcode=em-20250730-2&refcode2=383_1086043_pew6f_&akid=383%2E1086043%2Epew6f_ ]split $10 between my
team and Wes Moore to power our campaign to victory. But if you’re not
sure (which I understand!), here are five reasons I hope will convince
you:

1) New Jersey is not a safe Democratic state anymore — far from it. The
last governor’s election here? It was decided by 3%. New Jersey’s margin
in the 2024 presidential election? 6%. The first polling in this race of
the general election? It shows me leading my GOP opponent by only 3%.

2) Donald Trump is going to do everything he can to defeat me in this
race. He’s already endorsed my opponent, Jack Ciattarelli, and led a rally
for him — meaning MAGA money from all over the country is going to pour
into Ciattarelli’s campaign.

3) Unlike my opponent, I won’t ever hesitate to stand up to Trump when he
attacks New Jersey families. I’ve sworn an oath to the Constitution, and
I’ve spent my career honoring it to the best of my ability every single
day — before loyalty to any other politician or political party.
Ciattarelli has already made clear that his number-one priority is staying
in Trump’s good graces.

4) My top priority as governor will be making life more affordable for New
Jersey families. I’ve put forward detailed plans for lowering the cost of
everything from housing and energy to health care, child care, and
groceries — and I’m going to hit the ground running on Day 1 making them a
reality.

5) The stakes of this race are high not only for New Jersey, but for the
country. This is our chance to show the entire nation that the people
reject the Trump administration’s incompetence and authoritarianism. And
it’s our chance to get started on a better path forward — one where we
prioritize doing what’s best for working families over what’s best for
billionaires and corrupt political allies. There is no more important
bellwether ahead of 2026.

[ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20250730-2?refcode=em-20250730-2&refcode2=383_1086043_pew6f_&akid=383%2E1086043%2Epew6f_ ]If any of these reasons speaks to you, I hope you will split a
$10 donation between my team and Wes Moore to help me defeat
my Trump-endorsed opponent in this incredibly competitive election.

[ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20250730-2?amount=10&refcode=em-20250730-2&refcode2=383_1086043_pew6f_&akid=383%2E1086043%2Epew6f_ ]Donate $10 ››

Thanks for reading, and have a great rest of your day.

— Mikie

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:

# A New Banking Rule Could Reshape Retirement — Here's What You Need to Know
**New Rule Took Effect July 2025** My Dear Friend, Starting this July, a game-changing regulation is poised to reshape the financial landscape — and the biggest banks are already capitalizing on it. # Meet Steve Hilton
---
I love California so much. I moved to the Bay Area over a decade ago. I’ve raised my family here, taught at Stanford, started a business, written books, hosted a TV show ... lived the California dream. It’s my home, in the deepest sense. I’m a proud American, and an incredibly proud Californian too. But I’ve never forgotten where I came from. My parents were immigrants – they fled communism in Hungary to start a new life in England. In a free country. I appreciate exactly what that means.We didn’t have much money. My mother worked in a shoe store, my stepfather worked construction. My dad, who died when I was a kid, was the goalie for the Hungarian national ice hockey team. In 2012 we moved to California. I hosted a TV show — The Next Revolution with Steve Hilton — and podcasts: California Rebel Base, The Steve Hilton Show, Big Ideas Book Club. Through my policy organization, Golden Together, I’ve set out the changes we need to make to get this state back on track. Over the last few years, I’ve traveled the state, meeting people from all walks of life and backgrounds, in every part of California. I’ve spent time with business owners and workers in every industry, struggling with the absolute nightmare it’s become to start and grow a company here. I’ve seen the struggles so many Californians face raising a family given the unbelievable costs of living here. To make real change happen in government, you need the ability to think differently, the courage to challenge establishment groupthink and the conviction to follow through.That’s what I will bring to this job – to the urgent necessity of restoring the California Dream for everyone, and making this beautiful state, that we love so much, truly Golden Again.

**These are no ordinary times,****friend****.** I believe elected leaders should work to create safety, prosperity and opportunity for every American. Republicans in Washington don’t seem to share that sense of duty.
When I look at what’s happening in Washington now, lawmakers are tearing down our middle class to put even more money in billionaires’ pockets. They’re cutting critical jobs at agencies that help keep our country running. Not even our National Parks or Weather Service are safe.
_They’re punching down — attacking the most vulnerable among us — to make themselves seem strong._ Something has to give.
There’s another path, friend. When I was Governor of North Carolina, we _expanded_ Medicaid. We passed pay raises for public school teachers and we built a strong economy by investing in clean energy and investing in our people.
_Washington can look like this, too._ It’s time to elect leaders who are ready to do the hard work of strengthening our middle class, restoring voting rights and reproductive rights, protecting our environment and ensuring every child has the excellent education they deserve.
If this is the America you believe in, this campaign is for you, friend.

I believe that our brightest days are still ahead, but we have to work together to fix what’s broken in Washington. I’ve had enough. These are no ordinary times,friend. I believe elected leaders should work to create safety, prosperity and opportunity for every American. Republicans in Washington don’t seem to share that sense of duty. When I look at what’s happening in Washington now, lawmakers are tearing down our middle class to put even more money in billionaires’ pockets. They’re cutting critical jobs at agencies that help keep our country running. Not even our National Parks or Weather Service are safe. They’re punching down — attacking the most vulnerable among us — to make themselves seem strong. Something has to give. There’s another path, friend. When I was Governor of North Carolina, we expanded Medicaid. We passed pay raises for public school teachers and we built a strong economy by investing in clean energy and investing in our people. Washington can look like this, too. It’s time to elect leaders who are ready to do the hard work of strengthening our middle class, restoring voting rights and reproductive rights, protecting our environment and ensuring every child has the excellent education they deserve. body:
Hey Friend, it’s Brian Kemp.
I know most folks are focused on day-to-day life... work, family, everything in
between.

But I hope you’ll give me just a moment to explain why your support right now
matters more than ever.
<https://secure.winred.com/georgians-first-leadership-committee-inc/grassroots-victory-fund-investment-acs?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_acs&utm_campaign=20250728_grassroots-victory-fund-investment-future_acs&amtposition=2&utm_term=SDA>

This year, we’ve made major strides for our state and future...

From billions of dollars in tax cuts and refunds to budgeting conservatively
and streamlining government,we are putting money back in the pockets of
hardworking Georgians - providing real savings for them, their families, and
our state.

<https://secure.winred.com/georgians-first-leadership-committee-inc/grassroots-victory-fund-investment-acs?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_acs&utm_campaign=20250728_grassroots-victory-fund-investment-future_acs&amtposition=2&utm_term=SDA>
But if we want to keep winning and start delivering these results NATIONWIDE,
we cannot afford to slow down.

We need to start laying the groundwork for what’s ahead and it’s going to take
all of us working together to get the job done.
<https://secure.winred.com/georgians-first-leadership-committee-inc/grassroots-victory-fund-investment-acs?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_acs&utm_campaign=20250728_grassroots-victory-fund-investment-future_acs&amtposition=2&utm_term=SDA>

<https://secure.winred.com/georgians-first-leadership-committee-inc/grassroots-victory-fund-investment-acs?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_acs&utm_campaign=20250728_grassroots-victory-fund-investment-future_acs&amtposition=2&utm_term=SDA>
As Chair of the Republican Governors Association, I’m working to support
strong, conservative leaders across the country.

That starts this year — with key governor’s races in New Jersey and Virginia —
and ramps up in 2026, when 36 governorships will be on the ballot, including
right here in Georgia.

That’s why I’m building a Grassroots Victory Fund — a long-term investment in
outreach efforts, digital infrastructure, data, and tools to grow our movement
from the ground up.

Will you chip in $36 today to help NOW?
<https://secure.winred.com/georgians-first-leadership-committee-inc/grassroots-victory-fund-investment-acs?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_acs&utm_campaign=20250728_grassroots-victory-fund-investment-future_acs&amtposition=2&utm_term=SDA>

CHIP IN $36
<https://secure.winred.com/georgians-first-leadership-committee-inc/grassroots-victory-fund-investment-acs?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_acs&utm_campaign=20250728_grassroots-victory-fund-investment-future_acs&amtposition=2&utm_term=SDA>
Every single dollar you give helps us...

Elect more Republican governors in critical states.

Build winning campaigns in top battlegrounds.

Fight back against the Left’s radical agenda.

We’ve proven that conservative leadership works — but the future of our
country depends on whether we keep that momentum going.

RUSH $36 TO OUR GRASSROOTS VICTORY FUND TODAY
<https://secure.winred.com/georgians-first-leadership-committee-inc/grassroots-victory-fund-investment-acs?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_acs&utm_campaign=20250728_grassroots-victory-fund-investment-future_acs&amtposition=2&utm_term=SDA>
Will you step up today and help us build the strongest grassroots operation
possible?
<https://secure.winred.com/georgians-first-leadership-committee-inc/grassroots-victory-fund-investment-acs?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_acs&utm_campaign=20250728_grassroots-victory-fund-investment-future_acs&amtposition=2&utm_term=SDA>

Thank you for being part of this team, Friend.

Let’s Keep Choppin’,
— Brian Kemp

A MESSAGE FROM BRIAN KEMP

<https://secure.winred.com/georgians-first-leadership-committee-inc/footer-donate-page-acs?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_acs&utm_campaign=20250728_grassroots-victory-fund-investment-future_acs&amtposition=2&utm_term=SDA>

More than 35 years ago, I started my first business with nothing but a pickup
truck and a shovel.

Since taking office as Governor of Georgia in 2019, I’ve put hardworking
Georgians and their families first!

We’ve championed legislation to cut taxes for working families, crack down on
crime, end human trafficking, reform foster care and adoption, and support our
students and educators.

When Georgia became the first state to reopen during the COVID-19 pandemic, I
made sure we protected both lives and livelihoods. As a result, we’ve seen
historic economic investment, and we’ve continued to lead the way in creating
opportunities at every corner of the state.

And we’re not stopping there!

Marty, the girls, and I are working hard to ensure Georgia’s best days are
ahead of us.

But, we can’t do it alone. Our accomplishments are only possible with a team
of strong grassroots supporters likeYOU by my side. So, today I’m asking for
your support in my continued fight to improve the way of life for hardworking
families. Will you join me?
<https://secure.winred.com/georgians-first-leadership-committee-inc/footer-donate-page-acs?utm_medium=pemail&utm_source=rs_acs&utm_campaign=20250728_grassroots-victory-fund-investment-future_acs&amtposition=2&utm_term=SDA>

Thank you,
Brian Kemp

| | Today marks the 60th anniversary of the establishment of Medicare and Medicaid. Despite decades of American families relying on Medicare and Medicaid for literally life-saving care, Republicans in Congress have chosen to make the largest cuts in history to these critical programs under the Big Ugly Bill. **As a long-time advocate for strengthening Social Security and Medicare, I am worried about the consequences of the Big Ugly Bill and what it is doing to the millions of Americans who rely on these programs, especially our seniors.** Social Security and Medicare have served as lifelines, providing essential coverage and financial stability to our aging population, folks with disabilities, and lower-income families for decades. These programs demonstrate our shared commitment to ensuring a dignified life for _all_ , regardless of socioeconomic status. **When it comes to health care, I believe that access to high-quality, affordable care that fits Northwest Washington families' budgets is a right.** And for so many of our most vulnerable, that means utilizing Medicare. That is why I voted to:
* Reduce prescription drug costs by letting Medicare negotiate drug prices.
* Impose a tax penalty if drug companies increase their prices faster than inflation.
* Cap the price of insulin at $35 per month.
* Close a longstanding coverage gap in Medicaid that locks 4 million people out nationwide.
* Expand Medicare to cover hearing benefits.
* Lower out-of-pocket costs for Medicare Part D beneficiaries.
* Prevent the privatization of Medicare and ensure stricter accountability for private Medicare Advantage plans.

These are common-sense solutions that benefit _everyone_. Politicians in DC are running up our debt, ripping away our health care, disrespecting our veterans, cutting help for the poor and putting our Medicare at risk — just to give tax breaks to the very rich. I’ve had enough.
We have to change things, but I need you with me. Together, we can win this Senate race and help Democrats take back the majority. Julie Johnson (TX-32) is many things. She's a passionate advocate for reproductive rights and fundamental freedoms. She's an attorney who has fought for workers, students, women athletes, and folks with mental disabilities. She's a fierce legislator who has gone toe-to-toe with extremists in the Texas state House and then in the U.S. House. She's the first openly LGBTQ+ member of Congress from a Southern state. | | | | This morning, a member of the Texas House filed a proposed new Congressional map for Texas, which the House Redistricting Committee has indicated it will consider. The proposed new Congressional map is an affront to Texans in product, process, and principle. The map violates the _Voting Rights Act_ and the Constitution, diluting the voices of minority communities across Texas and dismantling districts that represent the political will of Texas voters. It is a betrayal of all Texans, no matter their political affiliation. It is a betrayal of the transparency and fairness of process that Texans deserve. And it is a betrayal of the fundamental organizing principle of a democratic society that all citizens should have a say in our government. Texans deserve better. I will continue to do everything I can to fight this redistricting effort as it moves forward, and I remain committed to serving the people of Texas’ Seventh Congressional District.

## **YOU’RE INVITED TO A SPECIAL ANNOUNCEMENT WITH CONGRESSWOMAN NANCY MACE**
I’ve always fought for what’s right, even when it wasn’t easy. Doing what’s right often means doing what is hard. Whether it was breaking barriers as the first female graduate of The Citadel’s Corps of Cadets, or standing up in Washington for lowering taxes, protecting women and children and bringing back law and order. I’ve done it for one reason: because **I love South Carolina.** But now, our state is at a crossroads. South Carolina continues to face the same challenges as we have for decades. And we ask ourselves, to what end? High taxes, turning a blind eye to sanctuary policies, allowing illegals to run wild in our state, few prosecutions if any, nearly last in the nation in education and the indoctrination of mentally ill ideology into our schools at every level. All paid for by hard working South Carolinians. Congresswoman Mace is considering a decision she never anticipated, but one she knows is necessary for the future of South Carolina.

body:
[ https://act.robbonta.com/go/4?refcode=em250729&t=1001&akid=1898%2E1088799%2E-TYRwA ]Rob Bonta

Donald Trump and congressional Republicans are
punishing Planned Parenthood for defending abortion rights.

In the process, they’re putting healthcare access at risk for millions of
lower-income Californians and Americans.

This attempt to strip Medicaid funding from Planned Parenthood is illegal
— so I filed a lawsuit asking the court to strike it down.

[ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-250729?refcode=em20250730-1898&refcode2=1898_1088799_-TYRwA&akid=1898%2E1088799%2E-TYRwA ]If you’re with me in the fight to defend essential healthcare and stand
up for Planned Parenthood, please split a contribution today between my
re-election campaign and Planned Parenthood Affiliates of California VOTES
PAC (ID# 1331005).

[ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-250729?refcode=em20250730-1898&amount=5&refcode2=1898_1088799_-TYRwA&akid=1898%2E1088799%2E-TYRwA ]Donate $5 »

Let’s be clear: this funding has nothing to do with abortion. That’s
already restricted by federal law. This funding goes toward medical
services like cancer screenings, STI testing, vaccinations, and wellness
exams — services that save lives, catch illness early, and protect public
health. For many people, particularly those in rural and underserved
communities, Planned Parenthood health centers are their only source of
care. Leaving them high and dry is cruel, and puts politics over patients.

The hypocrisy here is just staggering. The GOP claims to be defenders of
free speech — but only when it aligns with their own agenda. They say
they’ll “make America healthy again” — but they’ve repeatedly and
shamelessly made it harder to access healthcare.

California won’t sit back while Congress and this administration try to
roll back our progress, endanger our people, and ignore the rule of law.

[ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-250729?refcode=em20250730-1898&refcode2=1898_1088799_-TYRwA&akid=1898%2E1088799%2E-TYRwA ]Please stand with me by splitting a donation today — every
contribution goes directly towards the grassroots fight for freedom and
justice.

With this provision, Trump and Republicans in Congress are doing more than
blocking care to millions of people — they’re enacting a backdoor abortion
ban. Not by making abortion care criminal, but by defunding Planned
Parenthood and pulling essential funding from providers.

I won’t stand by while Medicaid — meant to uplift vulnerable communities —
is used as a political weapon in the GOP’s anti-abortion crusade.
Reproductive freedom and access to healthcare are human rights, and as
Attorney General, I will use the full authority of my office to defend
them.

[ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-250729?refcode=em20250730-1898&refcode2=1898_1088799_-TYRwA&akid=1898%2E1088799%2E-TYRwA ]I know you’re a committed fighter for reproductive freedom and access
to healthcare, so I hope you’ll stand up today by contributing to my
campaign and Planned Parenthood Affiliates of California VOTES PAC.

Thank you so much.

-Rob

[ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-250729?refcode=em20250730-1898&refcode2=1898_1088799_-TYRwA&akid=1898%2E1088799%2E-TYRwA ][IMG]

Rob Bonta

Democracy Docket: With New Order, Trump Tries to Kill Off Vote By Mail [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=073025_1&amount=25]
We're going to keep hammering this home, Team, because the mainstream media continues to ignore this executive order and how it will change our elections forever.
President Donald Trump's massive anti-voting executive order has sent lawmakers, election officials, and voting rights advocates into a frenzy. One provision focuses on a goal that for years has been a borderline obsession for MAGA: Cracking down on voting by mail.
For background: After every election in which he's been a candidate or in power, Trump has raged over the use of mail-in ballots in general and ballot deadlines in particular . He's tried to claim fraud for every single ballot counted after Election Day.
So of course, this order directs Attorney General Pam Bondi to “take all necessary action” against any states that count absentee or mail-in ballots received after Election Day.
This order makes it clear that the MAGA crew will do anything they can to codify their power permanently and silence the will of the people by suppressing and eliminating the votes we cast.
We've got to keep fighting and work to protect our elections and our fundamental right to vote. Step up with $25 or whatever you can today and help us defend vote by mail across the country >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=073025_1&amount=25]
